He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]]. He also represents the [[Serbia men's national basketball team|Serbia national team]]. ==Early life== Koprivica was born in [[Belgrade]] to [[Slaviša Koprivica]] and Tanja Čavić. Slaviša, who stands 6-foot-9 (2.06 m), is a former Serbian professional basketball player who won the [[1991–92 FIBA European League|1992 EuroLeague]] with [[KK Partizan|Partizan]]. Koprivica moved to [[Florida]], [[United States]] in 2012. In February 2017, he joined the [[Basketball Without Borders]] Global Camp in [[New Orleans]].{{cite web |title=NBA announces field of top international prospects for third Basketball without Borders global camp |url=https://pr.nba.com/bwb-global-camp-nba-all-star-2017/ |website=pr.nba.com |date=7 February 2017 |access-date=24 July 2021}} ==High school career== Koprivica began playing high school basketball in 2015 with [[NSU University School|University School of Nova Southeastern University]][http://www.maxpreps.com/athlete/balsa-koprivica/v9VhYkikEeS00gAmVebEWg/default.htm Balsa Koprivica, 15-16 Varsity Basketball] in [[Fort Lauderdale, Florida|Fort Lauderdale]], [[Broward County, Florida]]. He played at the 2015 [[Battle at The Villages]] high school tournament. In July 2017, he transferred to [[Windermere Preparatory School]]{{cite web|title=Five-star center, Koprivica, changes high schools|url=https://georgiatech.rivals.com/news/five-star-center-koprivica-changes-high-schools-1|website=rivals.com|date=9 July 2017 |accessdate=12 August 2017}} in [[Lake Butler, Orange County, Florida]]. He was considered one of the top ten [[College recruiting|college recruits]] in the class of 2019 until he dropped to a four-star recruit during his senior year.{{cite web|title=Dominant 7ft1 Balsa Koprivica Flashes Skills! Top 2019 Center|url=http://ballislife.com/balsa-koprivica/|website=ballislife.com|accessdate=12 August 2017}} In December 2017, he transferred to [[Montverde Academy]] in [[Montverde, Florida]].{{cite web|title=Montverde adds Balsa Koprivica for TV game vs. OCP|url=http://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/os-sp-hs-montverde-ocp-basketball-report-0110-story.html|website=orlandosentinel.com|date=10 January 2018 |accessdate=21 March 2018}} ===Recruiting=== On 26 October 2018, he committed to [[Florida State University]]. {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Balša Koprivica | position = [[Center (basketball)|C]] | hometown = [[Belgrade|Belgrade, Serbia]] | highschool = [[Montverde Academy]] (FL) | feet = 7 | inches = 0 | weight = 230 | 40 = | commitdate = 26 October 2018 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 | espn stars = 4 | espn grade = 88 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2019 | rivals ref title = Florida State 2019 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2019 Florida State Seminoles Recruiting Class | rivals school = floridastate | scout s = | espn schoolid = 52 | 247 overall = 93 | rivals overall = 88 | espn overall = 51 | accessdate = 6 July 2019 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Koprivica played his freshman and sophomore year with the [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]]. As a freshman, he averaged 4.7 points and 2.4 rebounds per game. As a sophomore, he averaged 9.1 points, 5.6 rebounds, and 1.4 blocks per game. On 13 April 2021, Koprivica declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |title=Balsa Koprivica to declare for the 2021 NBA Draft |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/1194521/balsa-koprivica-to-delcare-for-the-2021-nba-draft/ |website=eurohoops.net |date=13 April 2021 |access-date=30 July 2021}} ==Professional career== === Partizan (2021–2025)=== On August 23, 2021, Koprivica officially signed a three-year deal with his hometown and [[Slaviša Koprivica|his father's]] former club [[KK Partizan|Partizan Mozzart Bet]], under head coach [[Željko Obradović]].{{cite web |title=Sada je i zvanično: Balša Koprivica novi centar Partizana, ugovor na tri godine |url=https://mozzartsport.com/kosarka/vesti/sada-je-i-zvanicno-balsa-koprivica-novi-centar-partizana-ugovor-na-tri-godine/396532 |website=mozzartsport.com |access-date=23 August 2021}} His father was coached by Obradović, who played for Partizan (1991–1993).{{cite web |title=Slaviša Koprivica o sinu: Mene je u Partizanu trenirao početnik, a Balšu će najbolji trener u Evropi |url=https://mozzartsport.com/kosarka/vesti/slavisa-koprivica-o-sinu-mene-je-u-partizanu-trenirao-pocetnik-a-balsu-ce-najbolji-trener-u-evropi/396561 |website=mozzartsport.com |access-date=23 August 2021}} In his debut season with the club, Koprivica averaged 5.2 points and 3.9 rebounds over 33 ABA League games, but Partizan failed to lift any trophy. In 2022–23 season, his second with the club, Koprivica had his role reduced, appearing in only six EuroLeague games, but managed to lift the [[ABA League]] title with averages of 4.3 points and 3.3 rebounds over 12 games played. Over 2023–23, his role improved slightly, as he averaged 3.3 points and 1.7 rebounds over 14 EuroLeague games. The season was deemed to be unsuccessful for Partizan as they finished the season without lifting any trophy.{{cite news |title=Očekuje nas burno leto u Partizanu – ko ostaje, a ko odlazi? |url=https://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/srpska-kosarka/28999/ocekuje-nas-burno-leto-u-partizanu-ko-ostaje-a-ko-odlazi/vest |access-date=11 June 2024 |date=6 June 2024 |language=Serbian}} During the 2024–25 season, Partizan managed to lift the record eighth [[2024–25 ABA League First Division|ABA League]] championship, and the [[2024–25 Basketball League of Serbia|Serbian League]] championship, the first one after 11 seasons. === Bahçeşehir Koleji (2025–2026)=== On June 27, 2025, he signed with [[Bahçeşehir Koleji S.K.|Bahçeşehir Koleji]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/balsa-koprivica-signs-with-bahcesehir-koleji/|title=Balsa Koprivica signs with Bahçeşehir Koleji|last=|first=|date=June 27, 2025|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=June 27, 2025}} Over 15 games in the Turkish League, Koprivica averaged 5.7 points and 3.5 rebounds on 63.5% shooting from the field; with similar stats in the EuroCup. === San Pablo Burgos (2026–present)=== On August 3, 2026, he signed with [[CB San Pablo Burgos|San Pablo Burgos]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.acb.com/es/liga/noticias/balsa-koprivica-presencia-para-la-pintura-burgalesa-145726|title=Balsa Koprivica, presencia para la pintura burgalesa|last=|first=|date=August 3, 2026|website=acb.com|publisher=|language=es|access-date=August 3, 2026}} ==== NBA draft rights ==== Koprivica was selected with the 57th overall pick by the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in the [[2021 NBA draft]] and traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] for [[Mason Plumlee]] and [[JT Thor]], the 37th overall pick of the 2021 draft.{{cite web |title=2021 NBA Draft results: Picks 1-60 |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2021-nba-draft-results-picks-1-60 |website=nba.com |access-date=30 July 2021}}{{cite web |title=Charlotte Hornets Acquire Mason Plumlee and the Draft Rights to JT Thor |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/charlotte-hornets-acquire-mason-plumlee-and-draft-rights-jt-thor |website=nba.com |access-date=6 August 2021}} In August 2021, he joined the Pistons for the [[2021 NBA Summer League|NBA Summer League]]. On August 11, he made his debut in the Summer League in a 111–91 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]] in which he posted 2 points and a rebound in 4 minutes.{{cite web |title=91-111 Pistons @ Rockets Thomas & Mack Center, Las Vegas, NV |url=https://www.nba.com/game/det-vs-hou-1522100020/box-score |website=nba.com |access-date=11 August 2021}} Koprivica joined the Pistons for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web |title=Detroit Pistons 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612765/pistons |access-date=July 5, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} On June 30, 2023, the Pistons traded the draft rights to Koprivica to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] for sum of $2.1 million.{{Cite web |title=Home |url=https://twitter.com/home |access-date=2023-07-01 |website=Twitter |language=en}} On July 18, 2024, the draft rights for Koprivica were traded from the Clippers to the [[Utah Jazz]] as part of a deal centering on [[Russell Westbrook]] and [[Kris Dunn]].{{cite web|first=Gabby|last=Hundman|title=Utah Jazz Complete Trade with LA Clippers|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-complete-trade-with-la-clippers|website=NBA.com|date=July 18, 2024|access-date=July 18, 2024}} On February 4, 2026, Koprivica's draft rights were traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-koprivica-260204|title=Thunder Acquires Draft Rights to Balša Koprivica|work=NBA.com|date=February 4, 2026}} ==National team career== Koprivica was a member of the [[Serbia men's national under-18 basketball team|Serbian U-18 national basketball team]] that won gold medal at the [[2017 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]],{{cite web|title=Player Profile at the 2017 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship|url=http://www.fiba.com/europe/u18/2017/Balsa-Koprivica|website=FIBA.com|accessdate=12 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170812175200/http://www.fiba.com/europe/u18/2017/Balsa-Koprivica|archive-date=12 August 2017|url-status=dead}} with [[Marko Pecarski]] as teammate. Thirty years earlier, their respective fathers [[Slaviša Koprivica]] and [[Miroslav Pecarski]] had played together for the Yugoslavia under-19 national team, winning gold at the [[1987 FIBA Under-19 World Championship]].{{cite web|url=http://kosmagazin.com/koprivica-pecarski-30-godina-kasnije/|title=Koprivica-Pecarski, 30 godina kasnije|publisher=kosmagazin.com|language=Serbian|accessdate=August 12, 2015}} ==Career statistics== {{Euroleague player statistics legend}} ===EuroLeague=== {| class="wikitable" |- | style="background:#CFECEC; width:1em"|* | Led the league |} {{Euroleague player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2022–23 EuroLeague|2022–23]] | style="text-align:left;" rowspan="3"| [[KK Partizan|Partizan]] | 6 || 1 || 4.4 || .500 || .000 || .000 || 1.3 || .2 || .0 || .2 || 1.0 || .7 |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2023–24 EuroLeague|2023–24]] | 14 || 2 || '''8.3''' || style="background:#CFECEC;"|'''.833'''* || .000 || '''1.000''' || 1.7 || '''.3''' || .2 || '''.6''' || 3.3 || 3.9 |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2024–25 EuroLeague|2024–25]] | '''16''' || '''8''' || 8.1 || .600 || .000 || .800 || '''2.4''' || '''.3''' || '''.4''' || '''.6''' || '''3.4''' || '''4.1''' |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"|Career | 36 || 11 || 7.5 || .677 || .000 || .818 || 2.0 || .3 || .3 || .5 || 2.9 || 3.4 {{S-end}} ===EuroCup=== {{Euroleague player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2021–22 EuroCup Basketball|2021–22]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[KK Partizan|Partizan]] | 17 || 10 || 16.1 || .632 || {{sort|-|—}} || .600 || 5.5 || .8 || .5 || 1.2 || 6.4 || 10.1 |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"| Career | 17 || 10 || 16.1 || .632 || {{sort|-|—}} || .600 || 5.5 || .8 || .5 || 1.2 || 6.4 || 10.1 {{S-end}} ===Domestic leagues=== {| class="wikitable sortable" style="font-size:100%; text-align:right;" !
